summary: This work demonstrates teleportation of distance-7 topological surface codes on a 125-qubit superconducting processor, mapping out the phase diagram by tuning coherent errors and showing that the teleportation threshold increases from $0.122(2)\pi$ (at $\theta=\pi/2$) to $0.175(5)\pi$ (at $\theta=\pi/4$) through electric–magnetic duality symmetry. The experiment achieves logical error rates of $0.025(3)$ for Bob's teleported qubits and successfully teleports arbitrary logical states including magic states, validating operation below threshold with single-qubit gate fidelity 99.94% and two-qubit gate fidelity 99.64%.
motivation: Scaling surface codes for fault-tolerant quantum computation requires demonstrating robust teleportation of topological logical qubits across imperfect entanglement resources, which has not been experimentally verified at meaningful code distances despite being essential for distributed quantum computing architectures.
method: A tunable two-party state transfer protocol was implemented where Alice's distance-$d$ surface code (49 qubits per code) is teleported to Bob's initially product state by injecting coherent errors via parameterized $R_{XX}(\pi/2-2t)$ gates and single-qubit rotations $U(\theta,\phi)$, with tensor-network maximum-likelihood decoding applied to extract logical observables and measure phase transitions.
result: Below threshold at $t=0$, Bob recovers logical states with mean parity $0.68(8)$ and logical error rate $0.025(3)$; the coherent error threshold reached $t_c^{\text{exp}}(\theta=\pi/2)=0.122(2)\pi$ versus ideal $0.107\pi$, and increased 43% to $t_c^{\text{exp}}(\theta=\pi/4)=0.175(5)\pi$ at the self-dual point, with averaged magic-state fidelity $0.95(2)$ post-teleportation.
